description: 🚀 Somos Mineros del Espacio, un equipo del NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 en Málaga. Nos apasionan la ciencia, la tecnología, la exploración espacial y la creatividad. Queremos investigar las tendencias del sistema terrestre, descubrir patrones ambientales y transformar datos científicos en soluciones visuales e innovadoras. Buscamos personas con iniciativa y ganas de aportar conocimientos en programación, ciencias ambientales, análisis de datos, inteligencia artificial y diseño🌍⛏️
summary: Space Legacy is an educational Minecraft adventure (Java 1.21.1, Fabric + Ad Astra) that tells the story of NASA hardware left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Players travel to three worlds and recover the "echoes" of 16 real NASA machines: Surveyor 3, Apollo 11's Eagle, ALSEP, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Lunar Prospector, Viking 1 and 2, Pathfinder and Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10 and 11, NEAR Shoemaker, Dawn and Kepler. Each machine speaks in first person about how it worked and what it discovered, and passes "the baton" to the next mission, showing how each piece of hardware made the next discovery possible. A narrator, ECO, asks a short question for every echo, and players unlock mission files with NASA sources, museum rooms and 14 hidden real-world secrets. Designed for ages 9 to 14, it turns dense mission data into exploration and storytelling inside a game young people already love. Every fact was checked against NASA pages (NSSDCA, science.nasa.gov and JPL).
details:
WHAT IT DOES
Space Legacy is a story-driven Minecraft adventure built for the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten". The player follows ECO, the AI of an old tracking antenna that still hears the last signals of NASA machines. Across three chapters, each one a separate world, the player recovers 16 "echoes":
- Chapter I, The Moon (learning to arrive): Surveyor 3, Eagle (Apollo 11), ALSEP, Lunar Roving Vehicle, items left by astronauts and Lunar Prospector.
- Chapter II, Mars (learning to search): Viking 1 and 2, Pathfinder and Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight and Ingenuity.
- Chapter III, Beyond (learning to look far): Pioneer 10 and 11, NEAR Shoemaker on asteroid Eros, Dawn above Ceres and the Kepler telescope.

HOW IT WORKS
Each machine is a 3D model with 3 or 4 clickable parts marked with a yellow diamond. When clicked, the part "speaks" in first person (for example, "I dug trenches to test whether the soil could hold a lander") and ECO adds the scientific fact. After listening to every part, the player answers a multiple-choice question; a wrong answer explains why, with no penalty. Completing an echo gives a mission file (an in-game book with its NASA sources), opens a room in the Space Legacy Museum and reveals "the baton": the mission that continued its work. For example, the Apollo seismometers lead to InSight, which listened to marsquakes almost 50 years later. A quest book (FTB Quests) tracks progress automatically, and 14 hidden secrets reveal real but little-known facts.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT
Students usually hear only about active missions. Space Legacy makes the "forgotten" hardware visible, explains what each machine did and why it mattered, and connects engineering to the science it made possible. It uses a game many 9 to 14 year olds already play, so learning happens through exploration instead of dense documentation. Wrong answers teach instead of punishing, and there is no time pressure, which makes it accessible to younger players.

ACCURACY
Accuracy was our priority. We checked every fact, one mission at a time, against NASA pages (NSSDCA, science.nasa.gov and NASA/JPL releases). Claims we could not confirm in a NASA source were removed or replaced, and outdated facts were corrected (for example, Opportunity's driving record, which Perseverance surpassed in October 2026). The full fact-check log is included in the project folder. What is fictional is clearly stated: the narrator, the machines "speaking", and all sites being placed close together.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES
Minecraft Java 1.21.1, Fabric Loader, Ad Astra (rockets, oxygen, low gravity), FTB Quests, Just Enough Items and Controlling. The game logic is a Minecraft datapack of about 5,000 commands generated with Node.js (JavaScript) from a single content file, so facts are easy to edit and re-verify. The 3D models, the resource pack and the quest book are also generated by code. The demo video was edited with FFmpeg and its music was synthesized with code. The modpack is published in CurseForge format and as a one-click Windows installer.

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN CHOICES
The machines tell their own stories, with humor for younger players. The "relay" structure turns 16 separate missions into one narrative about how each discovery made the next one possible. A creative world lets teachers explore freely, and a survival world with a basic kit offers a full game experience. Our team signs the game with a plaque in each world. The game text is in Spanish, our local language; the demo and this page are in English.

Team: Mineros del Espacio (KGSMarie, Mariepeachx), Málaga, Spain.
